plugin.name: ida-ttd
plugin.description: Replay Microsoft Time Travel Debugging (.run) and Sogen (.sogttd) recordings as an IDA debugger session: step forwards and backwards, and query the whole recording for calls, coverage, memory accesses, syscalls and strings.

settings.name: Replay: start when a recording's database opens
settings.documentation: Start the replay as soon as a database made from a recording opens. Off: start it with Debugger > Start process (F9).

settings.name: Symbols: download PDBs
settings.documentation: Download the PDBs of a recording's modules from the symbol server, in the background, so system DLLs get their function names. Off: only PDBs already in the local store are used.

settings.name: Symbols: symbol server
settings.documentation: The symbol server PDBs are downloaded from (an HTTP or HTTPS URL laid out like Microsoft's).

settings.name: Analysis: highlight functions automatically
settings.documentation: Measure and colour each function the first time the replay stops in it.

settings.name: Analysis: resolve indirect calls automatically
settings.documentation: Comment the indirect calls of each function the first time the replay stops in it with where they went (one replay per module).

settings.name: Memory map: highlight executable memory outside modules
settings.documentation: In the Memory map, colour the executable regions no loaded module covers: code the program allocated or mapped itself, such as unpacked or injected code.

settings.name: Sogen: default fork length
settings.documentation: How many instructions the Fork dialog offers to record by default (decimal; 0 records to the end of the program).

settings.name: Sogen: registry hives folder
settings.documentation: Another folder to look for a Sogen recording's registry hives in, after the folder beside the recording and before ida-ttd\registry in the IDA user directory. Empty: none.

settings.name: Sogen: give forks and new recordings network access
settings.documentation: Let the emulated program reach the real network: a fork from its position on (the replay up to it stays offline), a new recording from its start. Off: a loopback-only network, where no host name resolves. The Fork and Record dialogs start from this and can change it.

settings.name: Sogen: checkpoint interval
settings.documentation: How many instructions apart a new recording or fork takes its full checkpoints (decimal; 0: Sogen's default, 500,000). Fewer checkpoints make a smaller file and slower travel.

settings.name: Sogen: record memory reads
settings.documentation: Keep every memory read in new recordings and forks. Off makes the file much smaller, but read breakpoints, read accesses and "where did this value come from" then find nothing.

settings.name: Sogen: record memory writes
settings.documentation: Keep every memory write in new recordings and forks. Off: write breakpoints, write accesses, strings, buffers and self-modifying code find nothing, and memory is known only at checkpoints.

settings.name: Sogen: record instruction fetches
settings.documentation: Keep every executed instruction's fetch in new recordings and forks. Off: coverage, execute breakpoints and self-modifying code find nothing.

settings.name: Sogen: record programs as administrator
settings.documentation: Run a program recorded with TTD > Record with Sogen... with an administrator's (elevated) token. Forks keep the token of the recording they come from.

settings.name: Sogen: show the emulator's log
settings.documentation: Print Sogen's emulator log and the program's console output in the Output window while a fork, a replay scan or a new recording runs. Useful when one fails or diverges.

settings.name: Diagnostics: write the log
settings.documentation: Write slow operations and session events to %TEMP%\ida-ttd-diag.log, which is what explains a hang after the fact.
